stem: Overbrook Data's internal analytics API on API Gateway gets an unpredictable burst of traffic from one internal reporting job every night, and the team separately wants a configured ceiling so requests to the API never exceed the account-level throttling limit AWS enforces for the Region. (Select TWO.)

choices.text: Increase the reporting job's EC2 instance size so it finishes faster
Remove all throttling settings so the reporting job is never throttled
Configure a stage-level burst limit sized to absorb the nightly reporting job's traffic pattern
Rely on the AWS account-level throttling limit alone as the API's only ceiling
Configure a usage plan quota for the reporting job's API key set below the Region's account-level limit

rationale: A stage-level burst limit is exactly the setting built to absorb a short traffic spike like the nightly job. A usage plan quota set below the account-level limit gives the team a configured ceiling instead of depending on the fixed AWS-side limit. Resizing the reporting job's EC2 instance does not change the API's request rate at all. Removing throttling settings removes protection instead of adding a ceiling. The account-level limit is set by AWS and cannot be tuned per API, so relying on it alone gives the team no configured ceiling and does not address the nightly burst.
